Standardize Path Coefficients onto Latent Liability and Common SD Scale

Source: R/standardize.R
standardize.Rd

Rescales parameters from a fitted because model or d-separation test into standardized path coefficients (\(\beta^*\)).

Usage

standardize(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'because'
standardize(
  object,
  method = c("error", "total", "mplus"),
  binary_predictors = c("raw", "sd"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted because model object or a because d-separation test object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

method

Character; liability/outcome variance calculation method:

  • "error" (default): Disturbance error + structural/random effects variance (\(\sum \sigma_{\text{random}}^2 + \pi^2/3\) for binomial; \(\sum \sigma_{\text{random}}^2 + \ln(1 + 1/\bar{Y})\) for Poisson; Nakagawa et al. 2017).

  • "total": Full McKelvey-Zavoina / Nakagawa total variance incorporating the empirical variance of the fixed linear predictor \(\text{Var}(\hat{\eta}_{\text{fixed}})\).

  • "mplus": Standardizes by the standard deviation of the linear predictions \(s_{xb} = \sqrt{\text{Var}(\hat{\eta}_{\text{fixed}}) + \sum \sigma_{\text{random}}^2}\), matching Mplus StdYX for Poisson regression (UCLA OARC FAQ).

binary_predictors

Character; scaling for binary/dummy predictors: "raw" (default; semi-standardization, keeping binary predictors on the 0-to-1 step so that the standardized slope represents Cohen's \(d\) on the standardized outcome scale; Gelman 2008, Bollen 1989, Grace & Bollen 2005) or "sd" (full standardization, scaling by \(s_X = \sqrt{p(1-p)}\); Menard 2004).

Value

An updated object of class c("because_standardized", "because") with transformed posterior samples and updated summary statistics. Fully compatible with summary, plot_coef, plot_rope, and plot_dag.

Details

  • Continuous (Gaussian) Variables: Scaled by the ratio of standard deviations \(\beta^* = \beta \times (\text{SD}(X) / \text{SD}(Y))\). If variables were already standardized prior to model fitting, their scale is preserved.

  • Binary / Categorical (Binomial/Bernoulli/Ordinal Logit): Raw coefficients sit on the log-odds scale. They are standardized a posteriori onto the continuous latent liability scale following McKelvey & Zavoina (1975), Menard (2004), and Nakagawa et al. (2017): $$\beta^* = \frac{\beta \times \text{SD}(X)}{\sqrt{\sum \sigma_{\text{random}}^2 + \pi^2/3}}$$ where \(\pi^2/3 \approx 3.289868\) is the theoretical disturbance variance of the standard logistic link.

  • Count (Poisson / Negative Binomial): Raw coefficients sit on the log-rate scale (\(\ln \lambda\)). Standardized onto the latent log / rate scale via:

    • "error" (default): \(\beta^* = \frac{\beta \times \text{SD}(X)}{\sqrt{\sum \sigma_{\text{random}}^2 + \ln(1 + 1/\bar{Y})}}\) following the GLMM latent distribution variance formulation of Nakagawa et al. (2017).

    • "total": Incorporates the empirical variance of the fixed linear predictor \(\text{Var}(\hat{\eta}_{\text{fixed}})\) alongside random effects and disturbance variance.

    • "mplus": Standardizes by the standard deviation of the linear predictions \(s_{xb} = \sqrt{\text{Var}(\hat{\eta}_{\text{fixed}}) + \sum \sigma_{\text{random}}^2}\), matching Mplus StdYX for Poisson regression (UCLA OARC FAQ).

  • Binary Predictors: Slopes pointing from a binary indicator (e.g. Migrant \(\in \{0, 1\}\)) to a response are kept on their natural 0-to-1 step when binary_predictors = "raw" (default), placing the effect on the standardized outcome scale (directly analogous to Cohen's \(d\); Gelman 2008, Grace & Bollen 2005). When binary_predictors = "sd", slopes are multiplied by \(s_X = \sqrt{p(1 - p)}\) (Menard 2004).

  • d-separation Objects: Evaluates and rescales each auxiliary independence claim across all d-sep sub-models, enabling a uniform rope = c(-0.10, 0.10) benchmark across all tests.

References

McKelvey, R. D., & Zavoina, W. (1975). A statistical model for the analysis of ordinal level dependent variables. Journal of Mathematical Sociology, 4(1), 103–120.

Menard, S. (2004). Six approaches to calculating standardized logistic regression coefficients. The American Statistician, 58(3), 218–223.

Gelman, A. (2008). Scaling regression inputs by dividing by two standard deviations. Statistics in Medicine, 27(15), 2865–2873.

Grace, J. B., & Bollen, K. A. (2005). Interpreting the results from multiple regression and structural equation models. Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America, 86(4), 283–295. https://www.jstor.org/stable/3868261

Nakagawa, S., Johnson, P. C. D., & Schielzeth, H. (2017). The coefficient of determination \(R^2\) and intra-class correlation coefficient from generalized linear mixed-effects models revisited and expanded. Journal of the Royal Society Interface, 14(134), 20170213.

UCLA: Statistical Consulting Group. How does Mplus calculate the standardized coefficients based on a Poisson model? https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/mplus/faq/how-does-mplus-calculate-the-standardized-coefficients-based-on-a-poisson-model/
